title: Espanyol Analytics: the new visual world
question: Your references are fixed in all of them: one continuous surface, a floating pill nav, borderless cards separated by tone, large light figures, one dark card per screen, the stadium photo. Each card shows the landing (highlight left, numbered index right). Choose one, steer, or re-roll.

options.label: Pizarra
options.lineage: the coach's magnetic tactics board in the dressing room
options.thesis: The site is the board the analysis is drawn on: flat panels on white enamel, possessions in marker strokes, players as magnets.
options.viewport: The stadium photo fills the top; the board rises over its lower edge. On the board, left: the season headline, key figures and the xG trend drawn as one blue stroke, plus 'Ver la temporada'. Right: index 01–05 as numbered exits. A pill nav floats over the photo.
options.risk: Push the marker idea too far (handwriting fonts, scribbles) and it turns into a costume; the strokes must be data, never decoration.

raised.raise: Depth comes only from flat panels overlapping, never from shadows or borders.
Every page ends in the same numbered exits (01–05), so the index is the site's navigation grammar, not a one-off on the landing.
One graticule: the 30-zone pitch grid is the layout grid every chart and panel snaps to.
Two inks only: Espanyol blue and marker red (opponent and negative) on the board; everything else is board tone.
One locked status corner: 'Datos hasta J7' always sits in the same place, never repeated in the body.

options.label: Grada
options.lineage: the stand at RCDE Stadium, blue seats with white ones spelling the club's name
options.thesis: The page is the stand: a blue field of seat blocks separated by aisles, with the numbers spelled in white like the mosaic in the photo.
options.viewport: The photo blends into a deep blue field. Left: the season's figures spelled large in white like the seat mosaic. Right: the index as stand sections 01–05. The pill nav sits on the roof line.
options.risk: Familiar: a deep club-blue site is where most football sites land, and white on blue gets heavy on long pages.

options.label: Telar blanquiazul
options.lineage: a jacquard loom, where punched rows add up to a woven pattern
options.thesis: The season is woven: each match a row, each possession a thread, and you can trace any part of the pattern back to the single action that made it.
options.viewport: Left: the season as a woven band, 45 rows (two seasons) of match threads, with the latest match lifted out. Right: the index as the loom's instruction rows 01–05.
options.case: Holds product clarity (pattern → row → thread is exactly Temporada → Partido → Secuencia) but loses audience identification: analysts and fans don't know looms.
options.risk: The metaphor can come before the football; it only works if every row is literally a match.

options.label: Fanzine riso
options.thesis: Two inks out of register, with a third colour where they overlap.
options.risk: Halftone breaks chart legibility, and it contradicts your clean tonal-card references.
options.case: Loses on both: it fights the references and the charts.
options.kept: Two-ink discipline: blue and red only.

options.label: Papercut
options.thesis: Depth made only by overlapping flat layers.
options.viewport: A symmetric roundel of cut layers.
options.risk: Folk ornament has nothing to do with football.
options.kept: Depth by overlap only, no shadows.

options.label: BBS
options.case: Off-audience, and its charts would be text art.

options.label: Oscilloscope
options.thesis: Every signal measured on one graticule.
options.viewport: A phosphor trace on a dark grid.
options.kept: One shared grid: the 30-zone pitch grid.

options.label: Broadcast signal
options.thesis: A broadcast falling apart on purpose.
options.risk: Noise is the opposite of rigour.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A modern football stats site at full craft: white ground, club navy, photo hero, clean data cards.
canonCard.viewport: Photo hero with headline and button, then a row of season figures and section cards.
canonCard.risk: Looks like FotMob or Opta Analyst by design; reads competent, not memorable.
